## Thinking

`split_think(text)` returns `(clean_text, thought)`. `clean_text` is the
reply with its leading `<think>` blocks removed.
[`thought`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#thought) is the
text of those blocks. Several leading blocks are joined with newlines.
Only a block at the start of the reply is thinking. A think tag that
appears after the answer has started, for example when the answer
explains the tag, is answer text and stays in `clean_text`. The function
also handles two damaged forms. If a leading `<think>` never closes,
everything after it counts as thinking. This happens when the reply ran
out of tokens in mid-thought. If a `</think>` has no opener before it,
everything before it counts as thinking. This happens when the chat
template already wrote the opening tag into the prompt.

### split_think

``` python
def split_think(
    text
):
```

*Split the leading `<think>...</think>` block(s) out of `text`,
returning `(clean_text, thought)`.*

``` python
test_eq(split_think('<think>weighing it</think>the answer'), ('the answer', 'weighing it'))
test_eq(split_think('no tags here'), ('no tags here', ''))
test_eq(split_think('\n <think>one</think><think>two</think>mid'), ('mid', 'one\ntwo'))
test_eq(split_think('<think>cut off here'), ('', 'cut off here'))
test_eq(split_think(None), ('', ''))
test_eq(split_think('weighing it</think>the answer'), ('the answer', 'weighing it'))
# a think tag after the answer has started is answer text
test_eq(split_think('write <think> to open'), ('write <think> to open', ''))
test_eq(split_think('use <think>x</think> tags'), ('use <think>x</think> tags', ''))
test_eq(split_think('<think>why</think>use <think>x</think>'), ('use <think>x</think>', 'why'))
```

## A call in the text

The body of a `<tool_call>` block should be a JSON object with a `name`
and an `arguments` object. The helpers below turn whatever the model
wrote into a tool call dict. The dict has the OpenAI form
`{'id', 'type': 'function', 'function': {'name', 'arguments'}}`.
[`mk_tc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#mk_tc) builds it.

Small models often write JSON that a strict parser rejects.
`loose_json(s)` tries strict `json.loads` first. Valid input is never
altered. If strict parsing fails,
[`loose_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#loose_json)
uses a tolerant reader. The tolerant reader accepts these mistakes:

- quotes inside a string that were never escaped
- raw newlines inside strings
- single-quoted strings and unquoted keys
- Python `True`, `False` and `None`
- trailing commas

[`loose_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#loose_json)
returns `(obj, complete)`. `complete` is `False` when the text stopped
before the object closed. A value that was cut off is left out of `obj`.
A half-written argument is never returned as if it were whole. Input
that does not start with `{` gives `(None, False)`.

### loose_json

``` python
def loose_json(
    s
):
```

*Parse `s` as a JSON object, tolerating common model mistakes, and
return `(obj, complete)` or `(None, False)`.*

``` python
test_eq(loose_json('{"a": 1}'), ({'a': 1}, True))
# an unescaped quote inside a value: the string closes at the CONFIRMED delimiter, not the first one
test_eq(loose_json('{"p": "say "hi" now"}')[0], {'p': 'say "hi" now'})
test_eq(loose_json('{"code": "a\nb"}')[0], {'code': 'a\nb'})   # a raw newline in a value
test_eq(loose_json("{'k': True, 'n': None,}")[0], {'k': True, 'n': None})
test_eq(loose_json('{"a": 1, "b": "cut')[1], False)            # ran off the end
```

A reply can be cut off inside a call. The arguments are lost then, but
the tool name usually arrived.
[`salvage_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#salvage_name)
reads that name. The caller can then report which call failed. The
function reads only the top level of the object. A `name` key inside the
arguments belongs to the data and not to the call.

``` python
test_eq(tc['function'], {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 1}})
```

Qwen 3.5 and later chat templates ask the model for calls in an XML
form: `<function=read><parameter=path>a.txt</parameter></function>`.
Claude uses a similar form of its own:
`<invoke name="read"><parameter name="path">...</parameter></invoke>`.
[`parse_fn_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_fn_tags)
reads both.

[`parse_fn_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_fn_tags)
decodes a parameter value that spells a JSON number, boolean, `null`,
object or array. Other values stay strings. The one newline that the
template puts on each side of a value is removed. Only parameters with a
closing `</parameter>` are kept. A cut-off call returns its name and the
parameters that finished.

[`parse_tool_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags)
tries this XML form before JSON. It reads a `<tool_call>` block that
contains `<function=` as XML. Text inside a parameter value is never
mistaken for the tool name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/tags.py#L197"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### parse_fn_tags

``` python
def parse_fn_tags(
    text
):
```

*Tool calls written in the `<function=name>` or `<invoke name=...>` XML
form.*

``` python
tcs = parse_fn_tags('<tool_call>\n<function=read>\n<parameter=path>\na.txt\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>')
test_eq(len(tcs), 1)
test_eq(tcs[0]['function'], {'name': 'read', 'arguments': {'path': 'a.txt'}})
# one framing newline per side is removed. The value keeps its indentation.
tcs = parse_fn_tags('<function=edit>\n<parameter=old>\n    indented\n</parameter>\n</function>')
test_eq(tcs[0]['function']['arguments']['old'], '    indented')
# no closing tag: the name survives, the finished parameters do not run
test_eq([(t['function']['name'], t.get('unread')) for t in parse_fn_tags('<function=edit>\n<parameter=old>\nx\n</parameter>')], [('edit', True)])
# an unclosed call does not borrow the closing tag of the next one: it is unread, and the next runs on its own arguments
txt = '\u003cfunction=a\u003e\n\u003cparameter=x\u003e\n1\n\u003c/parameter\u003e\n\u003cfunction=b\u003e\n\u003cparameter=y\u003e\n2\n\u003c/parameter\u003e\n\u003c/function\u003e'
test_eq([(t['function']['name'], t['function']['arguments'], t.get('unread')) for t in parse_fn_tags(txt)], [('a', {}, True), ('b', {'y': 2}, None)])
```

Some models drop the tags and answer with only the call object. The
object is sometimes inside a ```` ```json ```` fence.
[`lone_tag_tc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#lone_tag_tc)
accepts it only when all of these hold. The object is the entire reply.
The object has a `name` and an arguments field. When you pass `names`,
the name is one of your tools. A reply that describes or quotes JSON
fails one of these checks and does not become a call.

Arguments that cannot be read keep the call marked `unread`. They never
become a readable empty argument object.

*Read one bare call object. Mark unreadable arguments `unread`.*

``` python
test_eq(lone_tag_tc('{"name": "add", "arguments": {"a": 1}}')['function']['name'], 'add')
test_eq(lone_tag_tc('```json\n{"name": "add", "input": {}}\n```')['function']['name'], 'add')
```

Unreadable arguments in a bare call keep the call marked `unread`.

``` python
bad_lone = lone_tag_tc('{"name":"grep","arguments":"not JSON"}')
assert bad_lone.get('unread'), 'unreadable bare arguments must stay unread'
bad_lone
```

`parse_tool_tags(text, names)` is the function that a backend calls on a
finished reply. It returns the reply text with the tool blocks removed,
and the list of calls. It reads `<tool_call>` blocks in JSON or XML
form. It reads bare `<function=...>` and `<invoke ...>` blocks. It reads
a final `<tool_call>` that the model opened and never closed. The
bare-object fallback above runs only when no tagged call was found and
no block failed.

A model sometimes keeps writing after its last call. That text comes
before the result exists, so it is often a result the model made up.
[`parse_tool_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags)
drops all text after the last call. Text before a call and between calls
stays.

A model sometimes writes its own result markup, such as
`<tool_result>42</tool_result>`.
[`parse_tool_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags)
strips those tags. Their contents stay as ordinary text and never become
a call.

A damaged reply in the `<invoke>` form can leave `<parameter>` elements
between its calls. When the reply holds an `<invoke>` or
`<function=...>` call,
[`parse_tool_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags)
strips these stray parameters with their contents. A reply with no such
call keeps any `<parameter>` text that it quotes.

[`parse_tool_tags_ex`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags_ex)
does the same and returns a third value, `failed`. `failed` is `True`
when the reply held a tool block that nothing could read. Use it to tell
the model that its call was lost.

### tool_blocks

``` python
def tool_blocks(
    text
):
```

*The `(start, end, body)` of each closed call block in `text`. A JSON
body is read whole, so a closing tag quoted inside a string does not end
the block.*

``` python
# Claude's own form: `<invoke name=...>` with named `<parameter>` elements
inv = 'Reading both.\n\n<tool_call>\n<invoke name="view_file">\n<parameter name="path">/a/CLAUDE.md</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</tool_call>\n<tool_call>\n<invoke name="view_file">\n<parameter name="path">/a/notes.md</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</tool_call>'
txt, tcs, failed = parse_tool_tags_ex(inv)
test_eq((txt, [tc['function']['arguments']['path'] for tc in tcs], failed), ('Reading both.', ['/a/CLAUDE.md', '/a/notes.md'], False))
bare = 'Looking.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name="grep">\n<parameter name="pattern">x</parameter>\n<parameter name="regex">false</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>'
txt, tcs = parse_tool_tags(bare)
test_eq((txt, tcs[0]['function']), ('Looking.', {'name': 'grep', 'arguments': {'pattern': 'x', 'regex': False}}))
# a damaged reply leaves `<parameter>` elements outside any call. They are markup, not prose.
inv1 = '<invoke name="ls">\n<parameter name="path">/a</parameter>\n</invoke>\n'
stray = 'Listing it.\n' + inv1 + '<parameter name="1">\n</parameter>\n' + inv1 + '<parameter name="c2">\n<parameter name="path">/b</parameter>\n</parameter>'
txt, tcs = parse_tool_tags(stray)
test_eq((txt.strip(), len(tcs)), ('Listing it.', 2))
test_eq(parse_tool_tags('Write <parameter name="x">v</parameter> in the template.')[0], 'Write <parameter name="x">v</parameter> in the template.')

mangled = 'Reading it.\n<tool_call>{"name": "read", "arguments": {"path": "a"b.txt"}}</tool_call>'
txt, tcs = parse_tool_tags(mangled)
test_eq((txt, tcs[0]['function']), ('Reading it.', {'name': 'read', 'arguments': {'path': 'a"b.txt'}}))

cut = '<tool_call>{"name": "edit", "arguments": {"file": "x.py", "new": "def f(:'
_, tcs = parse_tool_tags(cut)
test_eq(tcs[0]['function'], {'name': 'edit', 'arguments': {}})   # the name without the half-written value

xml = '<tool_call>\n<function=read>\n<parameter=path>\na.txt\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>'
test_eq(parse_tool_tags(xml)[1][0]['function'], {'name': 'read', 'arguments': {'path': 'a.txt'}})

strargs = '<tool_call>{"name":"read","arguments":"{path: a.txt}"}</tool_call>'
test_eq(parse_tool_tags(strargs)[1][0]['function']['arguments'], {'path': 'a.txt'})

# a block that nothing can read sets `failed`
_, tcs, failed = parse_tool_tags_ex('<tool_call>{"totally": "unreadable"</tool_call>')
test_eq((tcs, failed), ([], True))

mixed = xml + '<tool_call>{"name": "ls", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>'
test_eq([tc['function']['name'] for tc in parse_tool_tags(mixed)[1]], ['read', 'ls'])
```

``` python
txt, tcs = parse_tool_tags('Let me look.\n<tool_call>{"name": "ls", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>')
test_eq(txt, 'Let me look.')
test_eq([t['function']['name'] for t in tcs], ['ls'])
# text after the last call is the model writing past it, such as a result it made up: it is dropped
ran_on = 'Looking.\n<tool_call>{"name": "ls", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>\n## Tool result (ls)\nnbs/05_git.ipynb\nIt is clean.'
test_eq(parse_tool_tags(ran_on)[0], 'Looking.')
bare_on = 'Looking.\n<invoke name="ls">\n<parameter name="path">/a</parameter>\n</invoke>\nIt holds one file.'
test_eq(parse_tool_tags(bare_on)[0], 'Looking.')
test_eq(parse_tool_tags('A.\n<tool_call>{"name": "a", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>\nB.\n<tool_call>{"name": "b", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>\nmade up')[0], 'A.\n\nB.')
```

``` python
test_eq(parse_tool_tags('just prose'), ('just prose', []))
txt, tcs = parse_tool_tags('<tool_call>{"name":"a","arguments":{}}</tool_call>'
                           '<tool_call>{"name":"b","arguments":{}}</tool_call>')
test_eq([t['function']['name'] for t in tcs], ['a', 'b'])
```

``` python
# invented result tags are removed. The text stays and no call is reported.
test_eq(parse_tool_tags('done <tool_result>42</tool_result>'), ('done 42', []))
test_eq(parse_tool_tags('{"name": "add", "arguments": {"a": 1}}')[1][0]['function']['name'], 'add')
```

A JSON call is read as JSON. When one of its string arguments quotes the
XML form, for example a model writing a note about the `<function=...>`
syntax, the quoted text is argument text. It neither invents a second
call nor replaces the real one.

``` python
xml_note = 'Syntax: <function=read><parameter=path>a.txt</parameter></function>'
note_call = '<tool_call>' + json.dumps({'name': 'write', 'arguments': {'text': xml_note}}) + '</tool_call>'
_, tcs = parse_tool_tags('Saving the note.\n' + note_call)
test_eq([(tc['function']['name'], tc['function']['arguments']) for tc in tcs], [('write', {'text': xml_note})])
L, R = chr(60), chr(62)
TC, TCE = L + 'tool_call' + R, L + '/tool_call' + R
FN = L + 'function=evil' + R + L + '/function' + R
THE = L + '/think' + R
b1 = TC + json.dumps({'arguments': {'text': FN}}) + TCE
b2 = TC + json.dumps({'name': 'a', 'arguments': {}}) + TCE + ' ' + L + 'function=b' + R + L + '/function' + R
b3 = TC + json.dumps({'name': 'edit', 'arguments': {'text': 'x ' + THE + ' y'}}) + TCE
test_eq(parse_tool_tags_ex(b1)[1:], ([], True))
test_eq([tc['function']['name'] for tc in parse_tool_tags_ex(b2)[1]], ['a', 'b'])
test_eq([(tc['function']['name'], tc['function']['arguments']) for tc in parse_tool_tags_ex(split_think(b3)[0])[1]], [('edit', {'text': 'x ' + THE + ' y'})])
parse_tool_tags_ex(b2)[1]
```

A weak model sometimes narrates a call (“I will now call
`{"name": "add", ...}`”) and produces no call that the parser accepts.
`tag_call_shape(text, names)` returns `True` when the text still looks
like a call after parsing. The text looks like a call when it contains a
`<tool_call` tag. It also looks like a call when it contains a `"name"`
that names a tool, together with an arguments key. Pass `names` to count
only tools that exist. Use the function to spot a model that does not
follow the protocol.

``` python
test_eq(tag_call_shape('I would call <tool_call> here'), True)
test_eq(tag_call_shape('maybe {"name": "add", "arguments": {}}', ['add']), True)
test_eq(tag_call_shape('maybe {"name": "add", "arguments": {}}', ['other']), False)  # no such tool
test_eq(tag_call_shape('plain prose'), False)
test_eq(tag_call_shape('{"name": "add"}'), False)   # no argument key, so not call-shaped
```

## Putting schemas in the prompt

`tag_tools_sp(toolspecs, sp)` appends a tool section to the system
prompt `sp`. The section lists the JSON schema of each tool inside
`<tools></tools>`. It shows the `<tool_call>` format. It tells the model
to send independent calls together, to stop after its last call, and to
never make up a result. Results come back in the next message under a
`## Tool result (name)` heading. With no tools, the function returns
`sp` unchanged. Pass `template` to use different wording. The template
must contain a `{tools}` placeholder. Write any other literal brace as
`{{` or `}}`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/tags.py#L336"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tag_tools_sp

``` python
def tag_tools_sp(
    toolspecs, sp:str='',
    template:str='\n\n# Tools\n\nYou can call the functions below. Their signatures are given as JSON schemas inside <tools></tools>:\n\n<tools>\n{tools}\n</tools>\n\nTo call one, emit a JSON object with the function\'s name and its arguments inside <tool_call></tool_call>:\n\n<tool_call>\n{{"name": "the_function_name", "arguments": {{"first": "value"}}}}\n</tool_call>\n\nCalls that do not depend on each other\'s results -- reading several files, running several searches -- go together in one message, each in its own <tool_call> block, one after another. A call that needs an earlier result waits for it.\n\nAfter the last </tool_call>, end your reply and wait. Nothing may follow it in the same message: not a comment, and not a guess at what a result will be.\n\nDo not describe a call in prose as well as emitting it, and never invent a result -- the real ones come back in the next message, each under a "## Tool result (name)" heading. That heading is the only form a result ever takes: do not write result markup of your own, do not wrap a result in tags, and do not copy a result back into your reply. Say what you concluded from it, not what it said.'
):
```

*Append the tool schemas and the `<tool_call>` instructions to the
system prompt `sp`.*

``` python
spec = {'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'parameters': {}}}
out = tag_tools_sp([spec], 'Be brief.')
assert out.startswith('Be brief.') and '"name": "add"' in out and '<tool_call>' in out
test_eq(tag_tools_sp([], 'Be brief.'), 'Be brief.')
assert 'one at a time' not in out and 'each in its own <tool_call> block' in out   # independent calls share a message
two = 'Reading both.\n<tool_call>{"name": "read", "arguments": {"path": "a.py"}}</tool_call>\n<tool_call>{"name": "read", "arguments": {"path": "b.py"}}</tool_call>'
txt, tcs = parse_tool_tags(two)
test_eq((txt, [tc['function']['arguments']['path'] for tc in tcs]), ('Reading both.', ['a.py', 'b.py']))
```

## Streaming

A tag can be split across two deltas of a streamed reply. A delta is one
piece of streamed text. For example, one delta ends in `<thi` and the
next starts with `nk>`.
[`StreamSplit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#streamsplit)
holds back the end of its buffer when that end could be the start of a
tag. It decides when more text arrives.

Call `feed(delta)` with each piece of text and call `finish()` at the
end. Both yield chunk dicts. Thinking comes out as
`{'channels': {'thought': ...}}` chunks. Answer text comes out as
`{'content': [...]}` chunks. The raw JSON or XML of a tool call is never
passed through as text.
[`StreamSplit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#streamsplit)
buffers it until the block closes. It then parses the block with
[`parse_fn_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_fn_tags)
and
[`mk_tag_tc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#mk_tag_tc),
which
[`parse_tool_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags)
also uses, and collects the result in `tool_calls`. The stream path does
not apply the
[`lone_tag_tc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#lone_tag_tc)
fallback. After the stream ends, `text`,
[`thought`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#thought) and
`tool_calls` hold the whole reply. `failed` is `True` if a tool block
could not be read.

The hand-written cases on this page cannot cover everything that real
models write. To collect real examples, set the environment variable
`URAI_RAW_DUMP` to a file path. A
[`StreamSplit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#streamsplit)
then keeps the raw text it was fed. The tool loop appends each such
reply from a chat with tools to that file. Each reply is one JSON line
that holds the tool schemas and the raw reply.
`tests/test_tool_traffic.py` replays captured replies through the
parser. `tests/harvest_tool_traffic.py` merges a capture file into the
replay corpus.
[`RAW_DUMP()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#raw_dump)
returns the path and reads the variable on each call.
[`dump_raw`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#dump_raw)
appends one record. When the variable is unset, each reply costs one
environment lookup.

### StreamSplit

``` python
def StreamSplit(
    keep_raw:NoneType=None
):
```

*Split a streamed reply into thinking chunks, text chunks and parsed
tool calls.*

``` python
def _run(deltas):
    "Feed `deltas` through a fresh splitter and return it with the chunks it produced."
    s = StreamSplit()
    chunks = [c for d in deltas for c in s.feed(d)] + list(s.finish())
    return s, chunks

s, _ = _run(['<think>', 'wei', 'ghing it', '</think>', 'the ', 'answer'])
test_eq((s.thought, s.text), ('weighing it', 'the answer'))
ordered, _ = _run([b2[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(b2), 3)])
test_eq([tc['function']['name'] for tc in ordered.tool_calls], ['a', 'b'])
ordered.tool_calls
```

``` python
s, _ = _run(['<thi', 'nk>deep</th', 'ink>done'])
test_eq((s.thought, s.text), ('deep', 'done'))
```

``` python
unclosed = '\u003cfunction=a\u003e\n\u003cparameter=x\u003e\n1\n\u003c/parameter\u003e\n\u003cfunction=b\u003e\n\u003cparameter=y\u003e\n2\n\u003c/parameter\u003e\n\u003c/function\u003e'
s, _ = _run([unclosed[:20], unclosed[20:]])   # an unclosed call followed by a complete one reads as it does in `parse_fn_tags`
test_eq([(t['function']['name'], t['function']['arguments'], t.get('unread')) for t in s.tool_calls], [('a', {}, True), ('b', {'y': 2}, None)])
```

``` python
s, _ = _run(['Looking.<tool_call>{"name": "ls", ', '"arguments": {}}</tool_call>'])
test_eq(s.text, 'Looking.')                       # the JSON never reaches the caller as text
test_eq([t['function']['name'] for t in s.tool_calls], ['ls'])
quoted = {'text': 'a </tool_call> "b" </tool_call> c'}     # a closing tag inside a JSON string does not end the call
sq, _ = _run(list('go<tool_call>' + json.dumps({'name': 'write', 'arguments': quoted}) + '</tool_call>'))   # one character per delta
test_eq(([tc['function']['arguments'] for tc in sq.tool_calls], sq.text, sq.failed), ([quoted], 'go', False))
sp, _ = _run([inv[i:i+7] for i in range(0, len(inv), 7)])   # Claude's dialect, cut mid-tag
test_eq(([tc['function']['arguments']['path'] for tc in sp.tool_calls], sp.text.strip(), sp.failed), (['/a/CLAUDE.md', '/a/notes.md'], 'Reading both.', False))
sp, _ = _run([bare[i:i+5] for i in range(0, len(bare), 5)])
test_eq(([tc['function']['name'] for tc in sp.tool_calls], sp.text.strip()), (['grep'], 'Looking.'))
```

``` python
s, _ = _run(['<think>cut off mid-thought'])       # unterminated: flushed by `finish`
test_eq((s.thought, s.text), ('cut off mid-thought', ''))
s, _ = _run(['<tool_call>{"name": "ls", "arguments": {}}'])   # unclosed, but parseable
test_eq([t['function']['name'] for t in s.tool_calls], ['ls'])
```

``` python
_, chunks = _run(['<think>why</think>because'])
test_eq(chunks, [{'channels': {'thought': 'why'}},
                 {'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'because'}]}])
test_eq(_run(['plain text'])[0].text, 'plain text')
```

The stream follows the same two rules as the finished-reply parsers. A
think tag opens thinking only before any answer text, and a JSON call is
read as JSON even when an argument quotes the XML form. Either way the
stream result equals the one that
[`split_think`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#split_think)
and
[`parse_tool_tags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#parse_tool_tags)
give for the whole reply.

``` python
note = 'Write <think> to open and </think> to close.'
s, _ = _run([note[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(note), 3)])
test_eq((s.text, s.thought), split_think(note))
s, _ = _run([note_call[i:i+4] for i in range(0, len(note_call), 4)])
test_eq([(tc['function']['name'], tc['function']['arguments']) for tc in s.tool_calls], [('write', {'text': xml_note})])
s.tool_calls[0]['function']['arguments']
```

Hosted APIs that support tools natively also stream them in pieces.
OpenAI sends each tool call as a series of fragments. Each fragment has
the `index` of its call. The first fragment holds the id and the name.
Later fragments hold more of the arguments string. `acc_tc(acc, deltas)`
adds the fragments of one delta to `acc`. After the last delta, `acc`
holds one complete call for each index. The arguments stay a JSON
string. The caller decodes it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/tags.py#L461"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### acc_tc

``` python
def acc_tc(
    acc, deltas
):
```

*Add streamed OpenAI `tool_calls` fragments to `acc`, one entry per call
index.*

``` python
acc = []
acc_tc(acc, [{'index': 0, 'id': 'c1', 'function': {'name': 'ad'}}])
acc_tc(acc, [{'index': 0, 'function': {'name': 'd', 'arguments': '{"a":'}}])
acc_tc(acc, [{'index': 0, 'function': {'arguments': ' 1}'}}])
test_eq(acc, [{'id': 'c1', 'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': '{"a": 1}'}}])
```

``` python
acc = []
acc_tc(acc, [{'index': 1, 'id': 'c2', 'function': {'name': 'b'}}])   # index 1 arrives first
test_eq(len(acc), 2)
test_eq(acc[0]['function']['name'], '')       # index 0 is a placeholder until it arrives
test_eq(acc[1]['function']['name'], 'b')
acc_tc(acc, None)
test_eq(len(acc), 2)
```
